figures.finding: From 2026 the first EUR 22,000 of a resident's taxable income is tax-free, then 20% to EUR 32,000, 25% to EUR 42,000, 30% to EUR 72,000 and 35% above; there is no regional or municipal income tax.

sources.said: Individual income tax rate Taxable income (EUR) Rate Up to 22,000 0% 22,001–32,000 20% 32,001–42,000 25% 42,001–72,000 30% Over 72,000 35%
Rates: The first EUR 22,000 of taxable income is tax free, with progressive tax rates up to 35% imposed on the remaining amount, as shown in the table above.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; employees and the self-employed without audited accounts file by 31 July of the next year, and the self-employed with audited accounts (turnover above EUR 120,000) by 31 January of the second year after.

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year.

must be filed by 31 July following the tax year for employees and self-employed individuals who are not required to file audited accounts, and 31 January of the second year following the tax year for a self-employed person whose return is accompanied by audited accounts. Self-employed individuals with annual turnover of more than EUR 120,000 must prepare audited accounts.

figures.finding: Employee and employer each pay 8.8% social insurance on earnings up to EUR 68,904 in 2026; the employer adds 1.2% redundancy, 0.5% training and 2% social cohesion (uncapped); health (GHS) is 2.65% for the employee and 2.9% for the employer on income up to EUR 180,000; the self-employed pay 16.6% social insurance on a notional income set by trade or profession, and 4% GHS.

sources.said: Social insurance fund 8.8 (2, 3) Redundancy fund 1.2 Training development fund 0.5 Social cohesion fund 2.0 GHS contributions 2.90 (3, 4)
the maximum amount of earnings on which the contributions are paid for 2026 is EUR 68,904 (weekly EUR 1,325 / monthly EUR 5,742)
The employee must also contribute at the same rate as the employer to the social insurance fund and the GHS fund at 8.8% and 2.65%, respectively
Self-employed individuals contribute at 16.6%. The contribution for self-employed individuals is calculated on notional income, which varies according to the trade or profession.
A resident individual is required to pay general healthcare system (GHS) contributions on various types of income (capped at EUR 180,000 per year) at rates of 2.65% or 4%.

figures.finding: The employer withholds tax from pay under PAYE; a self-employed person pays provisional tax in two equal instalments on 31 July and 31 December of the tax year.

sources.said: Filing and payment: Employers withhold tax on employment income under the Pay As You Earn (PAYE) system. Self-employed individuals pay tax through the provisional and self-assessment systems.
payments of estimated tax must be generally paid in two equal instalments on 31 July and 31 December within the same tax year.

figures.finding: The gross income a non-resident earns from a profession or vocation exercised in Cyprus, and the pay of a non-resident who provides public entertainment (a performer, a theatre or music group) for performances in Cyprus, is taxed at 10% of the gross; whoever contracts with the non-resident deducts it from each payment and remits it to the Commissioner, and the law levies no other income tax on that income, so the 10% is final.
figures.applies: Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002, arts. 23 and 24 (as consolidated on CyLaw).

figures.finding: Royalties paid to a non-resident for rights used in Cyprus bear 5% withholding on film royalties and 10% on others (treaties may reduce); no special treatment of a resident author's royalties was found.

figures.finding: VAT is 19%; a freelancer must register once taxable turnover passes EUR 15,600.

sources.said: Registration: The registration threshold for VAT purposes is EUR 15,600
The standard VAT rate in Cyprus is 19%.
